title: Mader's Conjecture (Conjecture 2)
statement_text: There exists a least integer $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(TT_k)$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\delta^+(D) \geq \mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(TT_k)$ contains a subdivision of $TT_k$.
context_text: Mader proved that $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(TT_4) = 3$, but even the existence of $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(TT_5)$ is still open. This conjecture, posed in 1985, is the central motivating problem of the paper, which seeks to verify it for special classes of digraphs.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture for all oriented paths (Corollary 20, with $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(P)=|V(P)|-1$), for all in-arborescences (Theorem 23), and for the union of two directed paths from $x$ to $y$ and one from $y$ to $x$ (Theorem 24); also studies an analogue via the dichromatic number parameter.

title: Conjecture 3
statement_text: There exists a least integer $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^0}(TT_k)$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\delta^0(D) \geq \mathrm{mader}_{\delta^0}(TT_k)$ contains a subdivision of $TT_k$.
context_text: A subdivision of a digraph $F$ is obtained by replacing arcs of $F$ by directed paths (internally disjoint, with new internal vertices). For a digraph parameter $\gamma$, a digraph $F$ is $\gamma$-maderian if there is a least integer $\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\gamma(D)\ge\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ contains a subdivision of $F$. Here $\delta^+(D)$ and $\delta^-(D)$ are the minimum out- and in-degree and $\delta^0(D)=\min\{\delta^+(D),\delta^-(D)\}$; every $\delta^+$-maderian digraph is $\delta^0$-maderian. This is motivated by Mader's theorem that graphs of large minimum degree contain a subdivision of $K_k$, whose naive directed analogue fails. $TT_k$ denotes the transitive tournament on $k$ vertices. Mader conjectured that every acyclic digraph is $\delta^+$-maderian, equivalently (as every acyclic digraph is a subdigraph of a transitive tournament of the same order) that there is a least integer $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(TT_k)$ such that every digraph with $\delta^+(D)\ge\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(TT_k)$ contains a subdivision of $TT_k$; he proved $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(TT_4)=3$, but even the existence of $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(TT_5)$ is open. This $\delta^0$ version is implied by Mader's conjecture and is in fact equivalent to it: if transitive tournaments are $\delta^0$-maderian then $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(TT_k)\le\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^0}(TT_{2k})$, by applying the $\delta^0$ statement to the digraph made of $D$ and a reversed copy of $D$ with all arcs from the reversed copy to $D$.

title: Conjecture 4
context_text: A subdivision of a digraph $F$ is obtained by replacing arcs of $F$ by directed paths (internally disjoint, with new internal vertices). For a digraph parameter $\gamma$, a digraph $F$ is $\gamma$-maderian if there is a least integer $\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\gamma(D)\ge\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ contains a subdivision of $F$. Here $\delta^+(D)$ and $\delta^-(D)$ are the minimum out- and in-degree and $\delta^0(D)=\min\{\delta^+(D),\delta^-(D)\}$; every $\delta^+$-maderian digraph is $\delta^0$-maderian. This is motivated by Mader's theorem that graphs of large minimum degree contain a subdivision of $K_k$, whose naive directed analogue fails. An oriented tree is an orientation of an undirected tree. A greedy procedure shows that every oriented tree $T$ is $\delta^0$-maderian with $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^0}(T)=|T|-1$, but whether oriented trees are $\delta^+$-maderian is open; this is posed as a natural important step towards Mader's conjecture that every acyclic digraph is $\delta^+$-maderian. As evidence, the authors prove that every oriented path $P$ is $\delta^+$-maderian with $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(P)=|V(P)|-1$, and that in-arborescences (oriented trees with all arcs directed towards a root) are $\delta^+$-maderian, which is not obvious since minimum out-degree gives no control on in-degrees; out-arborescences trivially satisfy $\mathrm{mader}_{\delta^+}(T)=|T|-1$.

title: Bermond–Thomassen Conjecture (Conjecture 5)
statement_text: For every positive integer $k$, every digraph with minimum out-degree at least $2k-1$ contains $k$ disjoint directed cycles.
context_text: Alon showed the weaker bound of $64k$ suffices; the conjecture asks whether the optimal bound $2k-1$ holds. It is mentioned as a related result about $\delta^+$-maderian digraphs; Theorem 8 together with known Erdős–Pósa results implies that disjoint unions of directed cycles are $\delta^+$-maderian.
paper_contribution: Mentioned as context; no direct progress, but Theorem 8 implies $k$ disjoint copies of $\vec{C}_2$ are $\delta^+$-maderian using the Erdős–Pósa property of $\vec{C}_2$ (Reed et al.) and the Directed Grid Theorem.

title: Alon's Partition Conjecture (Conjecture 6)
statement_text: There exists a function $h$ such that every digraph with minimum out-degree $h(k)$ has a partition $(V_1, V_2)$ such that, for $i = 1, 2$, $D\langle V_i\rangle$ has minimum out-degree $k$.
context_text: The existence of $h(2)$ remains open. If true, this conjecture implies Conjecture 7 that the disjoint union of two $\delta^+$-maderian digraphs is $\delta^+$-maderian.
paper_contribution: Mentioned as motivation for Conjecture 7; no direct progress made.

title: Conjecture 7
statement_text: If $F_1$ and $F_2$ are $\delta^+$-maderian, then the disjoint union of $F_1$ and $F_2$ is also $\delta^+$-maderian.
context_text: A subdivision of a digraph $F$ is obtained by replacing arcs of $F$ by directed paths (internally disjoint, with new internal vertices). For a digraph parameter $\gamma$, a digraph $F$ is $\gamma$-maderian if there is a least integer $\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\gamma(D)\ge\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ contains a subdivision of $F$. Here $\delta^+(D)$ and $\delta^-(D)$ are the minimum out- and in-degree and $\delta^0(D)=\min\{\delta^+(D),\delta^-(D)\}$; every $\delta^+$-maderian digraph is $\delta^0$-maderian. This is motivated by Mader's theorem that graphs of large minimum degree contain a subdivision of $K_k$, whose naive directed analogue fails. This would follow from a conjecture of Alon that there is a function $h$ such that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least $h(k)$ has a vertex partition $(V_1,V_2)$ with both induced subdigraphs of minimum out-degree at least $k$ (even the existence of $h(2)$ is open). A digraph $F$ has the Erdős–Pósa property if for every $k$ there is $\phi(k)$ such that every digraph either contains a subdivision of $k\times F$ (the disjoint union of $k$ copies of $F$) or has a set of at most $\phi(k)$ vertices whose deletion leaves no subdivision of $F$. The authors observe that if $F$ is $\delta^+$-maderian and has the Erdős–Pósa property then $k\times F$ is $\delta^+$-maderian for all $k$; with results of Reed et al. and Akhoondian et al., this shows that disjoint unions of directed cycles are $\delta^+$-maderian.

title: Burr's Conjecture (Conjecture 10)
statement_text: Every digraph with chromatic number $2k-2$ contains every oriented tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph.
context_text: The $\chi$-maderian digraphs are exactly the oriented forests (Theorem 9), but the precise value of $\mathrm{mader}_{\chi}$ is unknown. Addario-Berry et al.'s Conjecture 14 for oriented graphs implies Burr's conjecture for antidirected trees.
paper_contribution: Mentioned as motivation; Conjecture 11 is stated as a weaker consequence. No direct progress made.

title: Conjecture 11
statement_text: If $T$ is an oriented tree of order $k$, then $\mathrm{mader}_{\chi}(T) \leq 2k-2$.
context_text: A subdivision of a digraph $F$ is obtained by replacing arcs of $F$ by directed paths (internally disjoint, with new internal vertices). For a digraph parameter $\gamma$, a digraph $F$ is $\gamma$-maderian if there is a least integer $\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\gamma(D)\ge\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ contains a subdivision of $F$. Here $\delta^+(D)$ and $\delta^-(D)$ are the minimum out- and in-degree and $\delta^0(D)=\min\{\delta^+(D),\delta^-(D)\}$; every $\delta^+$-maderian digraph is $\delta^0$-maderian. This is motivated by Mader's theorem that graphs of large minimum degree contain a subdivision of $K_k$, whose naive directed analogue fails. Here $\chi(D)$ is the chromatic number of the underlying graph of $D$, and an oriented tree (forest) is an orientation of a tree (forest); the order of $T$ is its number of vertices. Burr proved that every digraph with chromatic number at least $(k-1)^2$ contains every oriented forest of order $k$ (improved to $k^2/2-k/2+1$ by Addario-Berry et al.), so oriented forests are $\chi$-maderian, and conversely only oriented forests are $\chi$-maderian (Cohen et al.). Determining $\mathrm{mader}_\chi(T)$ is open. Burr conjectured that every digraph with chromatic number $2k-2$ contains every oriented tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph; this statement, which only asks for a subdivision, is a consequence of Burr's conjecture and is proposed as an interesting step towards it.

title: Problem 12
context_text: A subdivision of a digraph $F$ is obtained by replacing arcs of $F$ by directed paths (internally disjoint, with new internal vertices). For a digraph parameter $\gamma$, a digraph $F$ is $\gamma$-maderian if there is a least integer $\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\gamma(D)\ge\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ contains a subdivision of $F$. Here $\delta^+(D)$ and $\delta^-(D)$ are the minimum out- and in-degree and $\delta^0(D)=\min\{\delta^+(D),\delta^-(D)\}$; every $\delta^+$-maderian digraph is $\delta^0$-maderian. This is motivated by Mader's theorem that graphs of large minimum degree contain a subdivision of $K_k$, whose naive directed analogue fails. The dichromatic number $\vec{\chi}(D)$ is the least $k$ such that $V(D)$ can be partitioned into $k$ sets each inducing an acyclic subdigraph, and $\vec{K}_n$ is the complete digraph on $n$ vertices (all $n(n-1)$ arcs). The authors prove that every digraph is $\vec{\chi}$-maderian; more precisely, if $F$ has $n$ vertices, $m$ arcs and $c$ connected components then $\mathrm{mader}_{\vec{\chi}}(F)\le4^{m-n+c}(n-1)+1$, which gives $\mathrm{mader}_{\vec{\chi}}(\vec{K}_n)\le4^{n^2-2n+1}(n-1)+1$. Since every digraph of order $n$ is a subdigraph of $\vec{K}_n$, $\mathrm{mader}_{\vec{\chi}}(\vec{K}_n)$ bounds $\mathrm{mader}_{\vec{\chi}}(F)$ for all such $F$, which makes its exact value the natural question.

title: Addario-Berry et al. Conjecture (Conjecture 14)
statement_text: Let $D$ be a digraph. If $|A(D)| > (k-2)|V(D)|$, then $D$ contains every antidirected tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph.
context_text: The bound $k-2$ is best possible. This conjecture for oriented digraphs implies Burr's Conjecture 10 for antidirected trees, and for symmetric digraphs it is equivalent to the Erdős–Sós conjecture. It characterizes $\bar{d}^+$-maderian digraphs (Theorem 13).
paper_contribution: Mentioned as context; no direct progress made.

title: Erdős–Sós Conjecture (Conjecture 15)
statement_text: Let $G$ be a graph. If $|E(G)| > \frac{1}{2}(k-2)|V(G)|$, then $G$ contains every tree of order $k$.
context_text: Addario-Berry et al.'s Conjecture 14 restricted to symmetric digraphs is equivalent to the Erdős–Sós conjecture. Ajtai, Komlós, Simonovits and Szemerédi announced a proof for sufficiently large $k$ in the early 1990s; partial solutions appear in the literature.
paper_contribution: Mentioned as an equivalent special case of Conjecture 14 for symmetric digraphs; no direct progress made.

title: Problem 16
context_text: A subdivision of a digraph $F$ is obtained by replacing arcs of $F$ by directed paths (internally disjoint, with new internal vertices). For a digraph parameter $\gamma$, a digraph $F$ is $\gamma$-maderian if there is a least integer $\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\gamma(D)\ge\mathrm{mader}_\gamma(F)$ contains a subdivision of $F$. Here $\delta^+(D)$ and $\delta^-(D)$ are the minimum out- and in-degree and $\delta^0(D)=\min\{\delta^+(D),\delta^-(D)\}$; every $\delta^+$-maderian digraph is $\delta^0$-maderian. This is motivated by Mader's theorem that graphs of large minimum degree contain a subdivision of $K_k$, whose naive directed analogue fails. Here $\kappa(D)$ is the strong connectivity of $D$ (the least number of vertices whose removal leaves a digraph that is not strongly connected) and $\kappa'(D)$ its strong arc-connectivity (the analogue for arcs). Since $k$-connected and $k$-edge-connected graphs have minimum degree at least $k$, Mader's theorem implies that graphs with large connectivity or edge-connectivity contain a subdivision of $K_k$; the question asks for the directed analogue. A conjecture of Thomassen would imply that all digraphs are $\kappa$-maderian: there is $f_1(k)$ such that if $\kappa(D)\ge f_1(k)$ then for any distinct vertices $x_1,\dots,x_k,y_1,\dots,y_k$ there are disjoint directed paths $P_1,\dots,P_k$ with $P_i$ from $x_i$ to $y_i$ (it would also imply Lovász's conjecture that highly strongly connected digraphs contain an even directed cycle).

title: Thomassen's Conjecture (Conjecture 17)
statement_text: There exists $f_1(k)$ such that if $\kappa(D) \geq f_1(k)$, and $x_1, \ldots, x_k$ and $y_1, \ldots, y_k$ are distinct vertices of $D$, then $D$ contains $k$ disjoint dipaths $P_1, \ldots, P_k$ such that $P_i$ goes from $x_i$ to $y_i$ for all $i \in [k]$.
context_text: This conjecture would imply that all digraphs are $\kappa$-maderian (Problem 16) and would also imply Lovász's Conjecture 18 about even directed cycles in highly strongly connected digraphs.

title: Lovász's Conjecture (Conjecture 18)
statement_text: There exists an integer $p$ such that every $p$-strongly connected digraph has an even directed cycle.
context_text: Stated as a consequence that would follow from Thomassen's Conjecture 17. It is mentioned as further motivation for studying highly strongly connected digraphs.
